summary: WebFetch worked for the large majority of this week's 45-record verification batch and for two discovery leads, contrary to the usual pattern of heavy egress blocking; a handful of domains still failed (zeet.co DNS, nexcess.net 403, namecheap.com 403, oracle.com 403, genesis cloud 503) and are omitted from checked_active entirely rather than guessed at. Four first-party-confirmed status changes surfaced: Cloudflare has acquired Deno (announced 2026-10-09 on deno.com's own blog), with Deno Deploy slated to shut down roughly six months later; Mistral AI is acquiring Koyeb per Koyeb's own changelog and site banner, with no immediate change for existing customers; CodeSandbox's own site now states it 'is now part of Together AI'; and Fleek's own domain now redirects to a bare 'something new, coming soon' teaser with its app subdomain returning 503, suggesting the live product is not currently operating normally. One identity change surfaced outside the rotation batch: a2hosting.com now 301-redirects to hosting.com, consistent with third-party reporting of a 2025 World Host Group rebrand; staged as an update only, since name/URL changes are never auto-applied. Two new candidates were verified by reading their own official pages: OpenSandbox, an Apache-2.0 AI-agent sandbox project, and General Compute, a GPU/ASIC inference cloud. Two other leads (AGBCLOUD, OpenRelay) were dropped because no official canonical URL could be confirmed (agb.cloud failed to resolve; openrelay.ai is a parked domain-for-sale page). 36 of the 45 rotation entries are reported as checked_active after reading each one's own current page; discovery searches covering serverless containers, AI sandboxes, GPU clouds, PaaS launches, self-hosted PaaS, edge compute, and hosting shutdowns/rebrands turned up nothing else meeting the bar for a sourced new candidate or status alert this week.

new_candidates.name: OpenSandbox
new_candidates.summary: An Apache-2.0 open-source sandbox runtime that gives AI agents isolated environments for code execution, file and browser/desktop operations, deployable via Docker or Kubernetes with multi-language SDKs and an MCP server.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams self-hosting isolated execution environments for coding agents, browser automation, or AI code execution rather than using a managed sandbox provider.
new_candidates.change_note: New open-source AI-agent sandbox project found via discovery search; confirmed via its own project site and GitHub repo, but confidence is kept low because the project site links to a GitHub org (opensandbox-group) distinct from the alibaba/OpenSandbox repo surfaced in search, and the exact relationship/governance isn't confirmed from either page alone.

new_candidates.name: General Compute
new_candidates.summary: A deployment service for heterogeneous AI inference hardware, pairing NVIDIA B300 GPUs for prefill with vendor inference chips (SambaNova, Cerebras, Positron, d-Matrix) for decode, deployed as dedicated racks in existing US colocation facilities under a single contract.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams wanting an OpenAI-compatible API or dedicated-capacity contract for high-throughput LLM inference without negotiating GPU and ASIC hosting separately.
new_candidates.change_note: New GPU/ASIC inference cloud identified via discovery search and confirmed by reading its own homepage directly; confidence kept low because the page itself does not label a formal GA/preview release stage for each hardware line, and only one first-party page was read this run.

updates.rationale: www.a2hosting.com now 301-redirects to hosting.com, a live independent hosting storefront with no reference to A2 Hosting. Matches third-party reports of a 2025 World Host Group rebrand of A2 Hosting to Hosting.com. Identity change (name/URL); staged for manual review only, never auto-applied.

status_alerts.rationale: Deno's own blog post 'Deno is joining Cloudflare' (deno.com/blog/cloudflare, dated 2026-10-09) states Cloudflare has acquired Deno and that 'Deno Deploy will continue operating for six months before shutting down,' with migration support offered to paying customers moving to Cloudflare Workers. The deno.com/deploy page itself also now carries a 'Deno is joining Cloudflare!' banner. The service remains generally available today; effective_date above is an inference (announcement date + 6 months) since no exact shutdown date was given on the page - treat it as approximate pending manual confirmation.

Koyeb's own site banner states 'Koyeb is joining Mistral AI to Build The Future of AI Infrastructure,' and its official changelog carries a 2026-02-20 entry titled 'Koyeb Enters Into A Definitive Agreement With Mistral.' Neither page uses the word 'acquired' or gives deal terms, and the page states existing customers see no immediate change, so status/availability are proposed unchanged; this alert exists to surface the ownership change for review, not a service disruption.

CodeSandbox's own homepage now states 'CodeSandbox is now part of Together AI!' and its footer reads 'a Together AI company.' Third-party coverage dates the underlying acquisition to December 2024, so this is a pre-existing ownership change not yet reflected in the catalog rather than new news; the product itself is operating normally, so status/availability are proposed unchanged pending a manual ownership/ entity review.

fleek.xyz now 301-redirects to fleek.sh, which shows only a teaser page reading 'We've been building something new. We're excited to share more soon' with no working product UI, pricing, or docs - just Discord/X links. app.fleek.xyz, the expected application dashboard, returned HTTP 503, and docs.fleek.xyz failed to resolve at all. This is firsthand evidence that the live product is not currently operating normally, but the page does not explicitly announce a shutdown or wind-down, so confidence is kept low/medium and status is proposed as 'transitioning' rather than sunset pending manual review.
